critique: The proved frontier is confined to a fixed arithmetic-mean closed e-test, known-variance local Gaussian outcomes, and a finite prespecified scenario list, so it is not a general subgroup-enrichment or joint test-design frontier. The computational result proves qualitative termination through exhaustive enumeration and diagonal refinement, but gives no complexity bound, convergence rate, implementation, or nontrivial interval-certified numerical instance; consequently the claimed rpact/interAdapt usefulness is not reproducibly demonstrated. The posterior-state reduction establishes initial-state Bayes optimality, while reusable value characterization after arbitrary interim states remains open because global generalized-terminal comparison and uniqueness are not proved. These restrictions leave a substantial and non-obvious diffusion-transfer and minimax-regret result, but cap its leading-journal significance and prevent flagship status.
